title: Citigroup Center
visualBrief: Detailed original Citicorp/601 Lexington exterior with four face-centered supercolumns and octagonal core, silver ribbon shaft, south-facing45-degree roof, separately modeled Saint Peters Church, stepped market and current sunken plaza.

sourceFacts.architect: Hugh Stubbins and Associates with Emery Roth and Sons
sourceFacts.renovation: Gensler plaza and six-story market repositioning; completed2021

reconstruction.tower: Independent mapped upper envelope retained above35m open underside. Fifty photographed office ribbon rows above the deeper transfer fascia; module datums are original reconstruction, not a floor-number survey. Hidden structural V braces remain enclosed.
reconstruction.roof: 915ft architectural peak, south-facing45-degree plane and flat end strips; two east louver slots and north antenna details follow LPC descriptions.
reconstruction.base: Independent mid-face columns, octagonal core, diagonally divided granite church, stepped market terraces and skylights.2019 LPC plan and2023 architect photograph guide the southwest sunken plaza.
reconstruction.facade: Continuous glazing/flat frames preserve silver ribbon cadence without repeated cell shells; supports remain separate from the raised tower.
reconstruction.plaza: Documented lower3.81m depression retains closed risers/retaining walls, open53rdStreet staircase, reconstructed furnishings/current food-hall exterior glazing. Ground streets/interiors excluded.
